Acme Dev: Hey, running into a weird issue with /rerank — after we started mixing precomputed embeddings from another provider with Redwood's reranker, the scores are all 0 or extremely small. No obvious 4xx from our side. Any ideas?

Maya (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the request body (redact secrets) and a request_id if you have one? Also which embedding model you used for the precomputed vectors and which rerank model you called.

Acme Dev: request_id=rc-20260305-9ab3
Here's the simplified curl we used (we precomputed candidate vectors with a separate embedding service and passed them in):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{
    "model": "redwood/reranker-1",
    "query": "How do I reset my password?",
    "candidates": [
      {"id": "d1", "text": "Click account > settings", "embedding": [0.001, 0.002, ...] },
      {"id": "d2", "text": "Go to /reset", "embedding": [0.003, 0.001, ...] }
    ]
  }'
```

We computed those embeddings with `openai-emb-ada-002` (1536 dims). The vectors we sent are length 1536.

Maya (support): Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) which rerank model exactly (you said redwood/reranker-1) — send exact model id/version if available; 2) do you see any error lines in the API response body (even if status 200)? Sometimes we return partial results with warnings.

Acme Dev: The response body is 200 but scores look like this: 
```json
{ "results": [ {"id":"d1","score":0.0}, {"id":"d2","score":0.0} ] }
```
No warning field. Model header: `x-model: redwood/reranker-1:2026-02-18`

Carlos (eng-oncall): tagging in. Quick hypothesis: embedding dimension mismatch. Our rerank models expect candidate embeddings to match the embedding dimensionality the reranker was trained/compiled against. If you feed 1536-d vectors to a reranker compiled for 1024-d inputs, math underflow/NaN can happen and older runtime paths used to coerce to 0 scores silently.

Priya (ml-eng): to add: `openai-emb-ada-002` is 1536 dims, while our `redwood-embed-1` families are 1024 (catalog note). If the reranker expects the latter but sees 1536 it won't align the dot-product/KV cache correctly. We should have produced a 4xx/422, but looks like this customer hit the silent path.

Maya (support): Carlos — can you check logs for rc-20260305-9ab3 and confirm whether runtime threw dimension mismatch warnings or an internal fallback?

Carlos (eng-oncall): pulled logs, snippet below (redacted):

```
[2026-03-05 14:22:10 UTC] request=rc-20260305-9ab3 model=redwood/reranker-1:2026-02-18 candidates_emb_dim=1536 expected_emb_dim=1024
[2026-03-05 14:22:10 UTC] runtime=WARN embedding_dim_mismatch; path=embedding_score; action=zero_out_scores (legacy_behavior)
[2026-03-05 14:22:10 UTC] response=200 duration_ms=42
```

Carlos (eng-oncall): So this confirms it. Runtime fell back to zeroing scores (legacy behavior). We're going to treat that as a bug — at minimum we should reject with 422 and an explanatory message.

Priya (ml-eng): Short-term workaround: re-embed candidate docs with the same embedding model we expect (use `/models` to check embedding dims or pass candidates as text so the server will embed them with the chosen embedding model). Example server-side call that avoids precomputed mismatch:

```json
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model": "redwood/reranker-1:2026-02-18",
  "query": "How do I reset my password?",
  "candidates": [ {"id":"d1","text":"Click account > settings"}, {"id":"d2","text":"Go to /reset"} ]
}
```

This will let rerank compute embeddings with the compatible model. Or re-run your batch embedding job using `redwood-embed-1` (1024 dims).

Maya (support): I've asked for a support-grade workaround and a timeline. Also creating an internal ticket to ensure we patch runtime to return a clear error. ticket-bot: create SUPPORT-3214, priority=P2, owner=eng-ml.

ticket-bot: Created ticket SUPPORT-3214 — "rerank: explicit validation for candidate embedding dims; disallow silent zeroing". Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUPPORT-3214

Carlos (eng-oncall): Plan: 1) patch runtime to validate candidate.embedding.length against model.expected_dim and return 422 with message like `embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1024 got 1536` (ETA 2 days), 2) add a rollout check to ensure older runtimes don't silently zero, 3) add a test in our e2e for precomputed embeddings.

Priya (ml-eng): Also pushing a doc blurb to dev docs and SDKs: detect mismatch client-side and raise before sending. I'll add a /models endpoint example showing dims so folks can match.

Acme Dev: Appreciate the quick triage. For now we'll re-run our embedding pipeline against redwood-embed-1 and retry. One question — will we be charged for the rerank call that returned zeros? It counts as usage on our invoice and we need to explain to billing.

Maya (support): Sorry — that shouldn't be billed as successful rerank usage if we failed the request on our side. I'll open a billing inquiry referencing rc-20260305-9ab3 and SUPPORT-3214 and loop in billing ops.

Carlos (eng-oncall): FYI internal note: if you need a temporary mitigation we can skip precomputed embeddings by sending text candidates; that will not incur precomputed-embed validation but will bill for server-side embeddings as normal.

Acme Dev: Got it. Re-embedding now. Thanks everyone. Will update here once we confirm results. :thumbsup:

Maya (support): Thanks — ping if anything flares. We'll track progress on SUPPORT-3214 and follow up when runtime is patched.

Priya (ml-eng): Follow-up checklist for eng/pm: add 422 validation, SDK check, doc update, billing note. I'll add those as subtasks on SUPPORT-3214.

Acme Dev: Re-embed completed — rerun succeeded, scores look reasonable now. Closing on our side but please keep me posted on the runtime fix.

Maya (support): Great to hear. Marking support thread resolved pending runtime fix.
